structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E026.
1. Correction from my misses. I kept anchoring time forecasts to old bases. E024, E025 and E026 were all measured against the current tip at that time (about 6.2 s, then 6.02 s). From now on, every forecast starts from the tip: E026, 6.017 s, 0.754. The code has 9.0 epochs, 225 steps, and resolutions 20/24/28/32 px at 0/15/40/70% of steps.
2. Resolution mechanism, refined. Low-res steps that come early are nearly free: E026 put 20 px in the first 15% of steps and lost no accuracy (+0.02 pp) for −3% time. Low-res steps that come late, or a large jump into the 32 px tail, cost accuracy: E011, E018 and E024 each lost 0.3–0.9 pp. My stem-miscalibration mechanism still fits this pattern:
   - The whitening filters are fitted on 32 px images, but most steps use downsampled images.
   - The whitening bias trains only during the first 75 steps, now all at 20/24 px, and then stays frozen.
   - The 32 px tail must re-adapt the stem and group 1 through BN.
   This predicts two things. Truncating backprop through group 1 in the tail (I043) hurts more than its FLOP share suggests. A cheap booster exists: let the whitening bias train again in the tail. The early phase could also go lower still (16 px for the first 10%) at little cost.
3. Noise. A rebuild moves the 3-seed mean by about 0.05 pp. Any change to RNG or step count is a fresh draw, with a 3-seed SD of about 0.25 pp. I put the tip's true mean at about 0.7545, so the margin is thin, close to a coin flip.
4. Hyperparameter plateau. Weight decay, label smoothing and Muon lr all land between 0.7537 and 0.7557. Muon renormalizes the filters, so filter wd is inert. The averaging ramp alpha² read +0.19 pp at equal time (E025). It is the one positive booster not yet stacked with a trim.
5. Epoch dial. About 25 ms per step at the current pixel mix, plus about 0.4 s fixed. Each −0.25 epoch gives about −0.15 s and about −0.12 pp.
6. Throughput. About 0.45 GMAC per sample forward at 32 px. Over a run that is roughly 880 TFLOP in about 5.6 s, which is above 100 TFLOP/s effective. No kernel lever remains (H6 is likely false, H2.2.4 likely true). Batch and step-count levers buy little time because the run is GPU-bound under CUDA graphs. Fewer steps likely cost accuracy, as with SGD.
7. Time model. Time ≈ steps × pixel mix + 0.4 s. The 32 px tail is about 40% of time.
Unsure: whether the stem mechanism is real (cheap to test); alpha² on held-out seeds; how results transfer to the PCIe judge.
Best path: alpha² plus −0.25 epoch, the whitening bias trainable in the tail, and maybe 16 px in the first 10%. Judge on 13 seeds.

forecasts.reason: Counting MACs and time gives above 100 TFLOP/s effective at 32 px, so the profile should show 90+ TFLOP/s and no big kernel lever.
I038 was discarded, so branch (b) runs: −0.25 epoch, about −0.15 s for about −0.12 pp on a fresh RNG draw. Keeping it is roughly a coin flip.
Saves about 0.25 s, but the 32 px tail exists to re-adapt the stem and group 1 after the low-res phases. Freezing them blocks that, so it loses more than 0.2 pp.
About 9% fewer steps saves time, but on CIFAR-100 with label smoothing, selecting on loss beats a plain epoch cut by little; the accuracy loss matches the epoch dial or is worse.
GPU-bound, so only the per-step Muon and overhead cost drops (about −3%). Twenty percent fewer steps and fewer Lookahead pulls likely cost about 0.3 pp.
The lr plateau is flat, as E014 (+0.09 pp) showed. ×2 is likely within noise, and possibly worse.

cruxes: Is the low-res cost a stem or tail re-adaptation effect? Test: on the E026 tip, does letting the whitening bias train again in the 32 px tail (or recomputing the whitening on the downsampled images) recover 0.2 pp or more at equal time?
Is early low resolution really free? Would 16 px for the first 10% (before 20 px) cut a further 2–3% of time with no accuracy cost, as E026 did for 20 px?
Does E025's alpha² gain (+0.19 pp) hold on held-out seeds 3–12? If so, it funds a −0.25 to −0.5 epoch trim at about −0.15 s per 0.25 epoch.
